title: Introduction to GraphQL
description: Understand GraphQL concepts, benefits over REST, and how .NET Core fits in.

data.text: **GraphQL** is a query language and runtime for APIs. Developed by Facebook in 2012, it lets clients request exactly the data they need — no more, no less.
Unlike REST, where you hit multiple endpoints and get fixed data shapes, GraphQL exposes a **single endpoint** and lets the caller shape the response.

cards.title: REST
cards.description: Multiple endpoints, fixed response shapes, over-fetching or under-fetching common.

cards.title: GraphQL
cards.description: Single endpoint, client-driven queries, strong schema.

data.text: .NET Core is a strong fit for GraphQL because of its strong typing, high performance, and rich ecosystem. The most popular server library is **Hot Chocolate**.

data.title: Hot Chocolate
data.text: Hot Chocolate is the leading GraphQL server for .NET. It integrates seamlessly with ASP.NET Core and supports schema-first, code-first, and hybrid approaches.

terms.definition: A contract that defines the types, queries, and mutations available in a GraphQL API.
A function that fetches data for a specific field in the schema.
A read-only operation that fetches data from the server.
A write operation that modifies data on the server.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GraphQL lets clients request exactly the data they need
It uses a single endpoint instead of many REST routes
Hot Chocolate is the standard GraphQL library for .NET Core
The schema defines the API contract
data.takeaway: Next, we'll set up a .NET Core project with Hot Chocolate.
